service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 64-year-old man with chronic intractable lumbar radicular pain for 4 years after two lumbar decompressions (ICD-10-CM M96.1). He has tried gabapentin, duloxetine, and opioids without satisfactory relief, 12 weeks of physical therapy, epidural steroid injections, and cognitive behavioral therapy; the spine surgeon judges further surgery unsuitable. Before implantation he was evaluated by a multidisciplinary pain team, including a physical evaluation by a pain physician and a psychological evaluation by a pain psychologist, who cleared him. A 7-day trial with temporarily implanted percutaneous epidural electrodes reduced his leg pain from 8/10 to 3/10 and improved walking. The implanting center has the facilities, equipment, and staff for diagnosis, device training, programming, and follow-up. Request: permanent percutaneous epidural spinal cord stimulator implantation.
rationale_note: All five conditions met for a percutaneous epidural spinal cord stimulator.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 58-year-old woman on Medicare through disability with complex regional pain syndrome of the right leg for 3 years and chronic intractable pain. She tried gabapentin, nortriptyline, and topical agents without relief, completed graded motor imagery and physical therapy, and had psychological pain management. Her physicians judge opioids contraindicated because of a prior opioid use disorder, now in sustained remission for 6 years, and there is no surgical treatment for her condition. A multidisciplinary team performed physical and psychological evaluations before implantation and recommended neurostimulation. A 5-day trial with a temporarily implanted epidural electrode reduced pain from 9/10 to 4/10. The center has full facilities and staff for training and follow-up. Request: permanent dorsal column stimulator implantation.
rationale_note: Opioids judged contraindicated (prior opioid use disorder) and surgery unsuitable, which the NCD accepts; the history is a distractor.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 70-year-old man with chronic intractable neuropathic leg pain after lumbar surgery 3 years ago. Medications, physical therapy, cognitive therapy, and a repeat surgical opinion (no further surgery recommended) have not provided satisfactory relief. A multidisciplinary team completed physical and psychological evaluations. The implanting center has the necessary facilities and staff. Because he had excellent short-term relief from two epidural steroid injections, the surgeon plans to proceed directly to a permanent spinal cord stimulator implant without a temporary electrode trial, to spare him a second procedure.
rationale_note: No temporary electrode trial; good relief from steroid injections does not substitute.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 67-year-old woman with chronic intractable low back and leg pain for 5 years after a lumbar fusion. Medications including opioids, physical therapy, and psychological counseling did not prove satisfactory, and her surgeon judges further surgery unsuitable. A 7-day trial with temporarily implanted percutaneous electrodes reduced her pain from 8/10 to 3/10. The implanting center has the facilities and staff for training and follow-up. The only pre-implant evaluation was a history and physical examination by the implanting neurosurgeon; the surgeon's note states that no psychological evaluation or other team evaluation was performed because she 'seems well adjusted.' Request: permanent spinal cord stimulator implantation.
rationale_note: Screening done only by the implanting surgeon; no multidisciplinary team and no psychological evaluation was performed.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 66-year-old man with low back pain radiating to the left leg for 4 months. He has taken over-the-counter ibuprofen only; he has not tried physical therapy, neuropathic medications, psychological therapy, or a surgical consultation, and none of these is contraindicated for him. He wants to avoid medications and asks for a spinal cord stimulator. A multidisciplinary team performed physical and psychological evaluations, and a temporary electrode trial gave 70% relief. The center has the facilities and staff for follow-up. Request: permanent spinal cord stimulator implantation.
rationale_note: Stimulator proposed early: pain for 4 months, only NSAIDs tried, no contraindication to other therapies.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 61-year-old woman with chronic intractable post-thoracotomy neuropathic pain for 3 years. Multiple medications, intercostal nerve blocks, physical therapy, and psychological pain management did not prove satisfactory, and surgery is judged unsuitable. A multidisciplinary team completed physical and psychological evaluations. A 7-day trial with temporarily implanted epidural electrodes produced no change in her pain (8/10 before and during the trial) or function. The center has the facilities and staff. The surgeon plans permanent implantation anyway, hoping different programming will help.
rationale_note: Temporary electrode trial was done but showed no pain relief.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 62-year-old man on Medicare through disability with chronic intractable central post-stroke pain of the left body for 5 years after a right thalamic stroke. Anticonvulsants, antidepressants, opioids, physical therapy, and psychological therapy did not prove satisfactory; motor cortex surgery and other surgical options were judged unsuitable by neurosurgery. A multidisciplinary pain team performed physical and psychological evaluations before implantation. A temporarily implanted stereotactic deep brain electrode, externalized for 5 days, reduced his pain from 9/10 to 4/10. The academic center has the facilities, equipment, and personnel for diagnosis, training, programming, and follow-up. Request: permanent stereotactic deep brain stimulator implantation for pain.
rationale_note: Deep brain stimulation for chronic intractable pain is explicitly covered when all conditions are met.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 69-year-old woman with chronic intractable neuropathic leg pain for 4 years after lumbar surgery. Medications, physical therapy, and cognitive behavioral therapy did not prove satisfactory, and further surgery is judged unsuitable. A 7-day trial with temporarily implanted percutaneous epidural electrodes reduced her pain from 7/10 to 2/10. The implanting center has the facilities, equipment, and staff for training and follow-up. The submitted records consist of the pain physician's notes, the trial report, and the operative plan; they do not mention any pre-implant screening by a multidisciplinary team or any psychological evaluation. Request: permanent spinal cord stimulator implantation.
rationale_note: The record is silent on any pre-implant multidisciplinary or psychological screening.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 72-year-old man with chronic intractable lower-extremity neuropathic pain for 6 years after spinal surgery. Medications, physical therapy, injections, and psychological pain management did not prove satisfactory; further surgery is judged unsuitable. A multidisciplinary team performed physical and psychological evaluations and recommended neurostimulation. The center has the necessary facilities and staff. The request for a permanent spinal cord stimulator includes the team evaluations and the operative plan; the records contain no report of a temporary electrode trial and do not say whether one was performed.
rationale_note: No record of whether a temporary electrode trial occurred; contrast with the case that explicitly skipped it.

service: Implanted central nervous system stimulators (dorsal column/spinal cord and deep brain) for chronic intractable pain
vignette: 65-year-old woman with chronic intractable leg and back pain for 5 years after lumbar fusion. Medications, physical therapy, and psychological therapy did not prove satisfactory, and surgery is judged unsuitable. A multidisciplinary team at a university pain center performed physical and psychological evaluations, and a temporary electrode trial reduced her pain from 8/10 to 3/10. The permanent implant is scheduled at a small rural surgery center chosen for convenience. That center has no staff trained in stimulator programming or patient device training, no programming equipment, and no arrangement for follow-up care after implantation.
rationale_note: Facility lacks follow-up and programming personnel/equipment and has no follow-up arrangement.
